claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: For two same-supply flows x,y, conservation cancels all nonterminal terms in the harmonic weighted edge sum, giving x^-(t)-y^-(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)-d_x(v))g_t(v). Harmonicity gives g_t(v)=(h_t(s_1(v))-h_t(s_0(v)))/2, so |g_t(v)|≤1/2 and every terminal-coordinate diameter is at most N/2. Total terminal inflow is fixed by conservation; hence the first |T|-1 integral coordinates each have at most floor(N/2)+1 possibilities, proving a polynomial bound for fixed |T|. The asserted exactness for two terminals and unit supply is also valid: transience makes the relevant linear system invertible, and every d∈[0,1]^N yields nonnegative flows; choosing the two endpoint d-vectors according to sign(g) attains Σ|g|.
claims.search_method: Direct summation-by-parts proof, conservation check, and exact-rational tests of the prescribed-imbalance realization.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: An edge from level i cannot go below level i-1. Consequently, a zero-player walk starting at level at least i hits L_{i-1} before absorption. Since the finite walk is transient, first-hit decomposition expresses its hitting probability as a convex combination of values on L_{i-1}. This proves m_{i-1}≤m_i≤M_i≤M_{i-1}. Both successors of v∈L_i therefore have values in [m_{i-1},M_{i-1}], yielding |g(v)|≤W_{i-1}/2 and Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_iW_{i-1}. The width-three family in claim 2 has gap mass Θ(k), proving that linear growth can actually occur.
claims.witness: The k-level width-three family from claim 2 has gap mass k(k+7)/(4(k+1))=Θ(k).
claims.search_method: First-hit harmonic analysis followed by exact-rational evaluation of the parametric family.

claims.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
claims.evidence: Substitution in the stated family gives h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1-i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. Summing the resulting exact gaps gives k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). Unit supply realizes both sign-selected imbalance vectors, so harmonic duality attains this entire sink-inflow separation. For k=2, every listed edge value is nonnegative, every even-minus-odd imbalance lies in [0,1], every nonsink has outflow minus inflow exactly 1, and the sink-1 inflows are 10/3 and 11/6, differing by 3/2>1. Padding each level gives the stated fixed-width extension and gap formula.
claims.witness: The explicit k=2 flows in the draft share unit supply and have sink-1 inflows 10/3 and 11/6.
claims.search_method: Exact algebraic derivation plus Fraction-based validation for k=2 through 14 and widths 3 through 8.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
claims.evidence: Both completions are simple binary graphs with exactly three vertices at each positive level and identical outgoing edges from L_1. Solving their harmonic equations exactly gives completion A: (h(a),h(b))=(3/22,1/22), and completion B: (h(a),h(b))=(1/22,3/22). Thus identical preceding-level order and identical current-level outgoing data lead to opposite within-level orders, establishing the precise local non-determinacy asserted by the proof sketch.
claims.witness: Completion A uses X→(c,b), Y→(a,b); completion B uses X→(a,b), Y→(c,a), with all common edges as listed in the draft.
claims.search_method: Exact Gaussian elimination over rational numbers and directed-distance validation.

claims.claim: For fixed supply and a fixed number of terminals, all feasible integral boundary signatures of real switching flows can be enumerated in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: The feasible-flow set is a rational polyhedron. Terminal inflows are bounded because they are nonnegative and sum to the integral total supply. Exact rational LP computes each coordinate minimum and maximum, while claim 0 bounds every range length by N/2. Thus only polynomially many integer tuples for the first fixed number minus one terminal coordinates need testing. Conservation forces the last coordinate, and one rational LP with terminal equalities decides each tuple. LP bit complexity and candidate integer bit lengths remain polynomial in the input encoding. This enumerates integral boundary vectors of real flows and does not incorrectly assert edge integrality.
claims.search_method: Direct rational-polyhedral, output-size, and Turing bit-complexity analysis.

claims.claim: At positive-level width three, one fixed integer supply can admit Θ(N) distinct integral sink-inflow signatures among real switching flows.
claims.evidence: For N=3k, the two unit-supply flows from claim 2 have sink-1 inflows separated by D=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(N). The real switching-flow region is convex, so convex combinations realize every real sink-1 inflow in the closed interval between them. Every integer q in that interval produces the integral two-terminal signature (N-q,q); the interval contains at least floor(D)=Θ(N) such integers. Claim 0 gives the matching O(N) upper bound. Exact interpolation checks confirmed conservation, nonnegativity, switching inequalities, and each resulting signature.
claims.witness: The width-three k-level family with φ(v)=1 for every nonsink.
claims.search_method: Convexity proof and exact-rational construction of all intermediate integral signatures for k=2 through 14.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether ARRIVAL is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed level width r>2, beginning with r=3. Under the source definition, L_0 always contains the two sinks, so the literal phrase “every nonempty levelset” would make the r>2 class empty; the draft reasonably addresses the intended positive-level interpretation instead of claiming a vacuous solution. On that interpretation, it supplies neither a polynomial-time ARRIVAL algorithm nor a contrary classification, so it does not fully resolve the target. Its verified boundary-signature bound and width-three counterexamples are nevertheless material structural progress. The final writeup expressly acknowledges the unresolved varying-supply obstacle and makes no headline claim of full coverage. Therefore VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate and the draft's claimed resolution PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
